title: SF-A09-T03.1: Complete scalar StringWriter writes and string-line disposal order
head: codex/a09-string-writer-scalars
body:
Task: SF-A09-T03.1

Related to #2723; it remains open for the remaining text-IO surface.

**Stack:** base is `codex/a09-string-writer-char-line` (#4517), above #4509 → #4510 → #4513 → #4514 → #4515 → #4516 → #4517. Merge those prerequisites in order with merge commits.

## Completed batch

Add all sixteen scalar `StringWriter.Write` / `WriteLine` contracts for Boolean, Int32, UInt32, Int64, UInt64, Single, Double and Decimal (append-only IDs 655388–655403). Reuse the typed StringBuilder append handlers and exact managed scalar carriers through a cached immutable dispatch map. Receiver, builder and boxed value roots survive allocation callbacks and collection.

The value is written before WriteLine rereads disposal and the current NewLine. Native captures exposed the same missing second disposal check in the existing string WriteLine path; this batch fixes that path too. Disposal during a value append prevents the newline while retaining the written value. Null strings write only the newline, and disposal after the completed newline remains allowed.

One older string-line assertion encoded the incorrect ordering and is replaced with the pinned native expectation. The new string-line regression failed four of twelve cases on its immediate pre-fix revision and passes after the fix.

## Reference and validation

Real captures executed with .NET SDK **10.0.201 / CoreCLR 10.0.5**, Linux x64, using the committed native programs and offline package configuration:
- Scalars: **312 ordinary rows + 24 callback-transition rows**.
- String WriteLine: **144 ordinary rows + 36 callback-transition rows**.

Committed source and capture digests are verified by the focused tests. Source and legacy compiler pipelines and the JavaScript source/CIL runtimes are covered, including independently authored CIL, receiver/disposal errors, numeric widths, non-finite values, capacity failures, GC/root lifetimes, NewLine changes and callback ordering. These counts describe native vectors; the Node test count below describes test cases.

At local commit `59971677f58bc4bc947e6702ccd82670f915c5bb`:
- **244 affected tests passed, 0 failed/cancelled/skipped/todo**.
- `npm run check`: 30 area manifests, 1,015 Node files, zero unassigned/duplicate owners; 3,707 syntax modules, zero syntax errors; 3,703 static imports, zero errors.
- Structure check passed with existing repository baseline warnings.
- Browser application build passed.
- Earlier scalar revision `8c12e56` passed the isolated all-workspace tarball install and package smoke check. That packaging check was not rerun after the small string-line gate correction.
- Clean `npm ci` remains blocked by the inherited workspace lockfile omission below; local workspace setup used `--package-lock=false`. This is not claimed as a clean-install pass.

Published commit: `c01f8b5bede834b067a270a105edd2e059355157`. **Exact source tree shared with the tested local commit:** `5d8fa810876460a0a09cdbf412849ee5bae91f63`. Connector publication creates new commit metadata, and the full tree is verified identical.

## Performance and size: review required

Node 24.19.0, Linux x64, AMD EPYC 9V74, shared host, team's heavy jobs serial. The committed runner uses 27 unchanged controls and 24 new scalar workloads per engine, one warmup and five samples. Runner SHA-256 `972c12f59b0692b6297f1c1ded1fffd1da7283e37302ca40ae3356c60aa60674`.

Two complete before/after comparisons were retained. The first used 64 calls / 1,024 stress units; it showed 25–70% median increases in several short controls. The second used 256 calls / 256 stress units and reversed many of those changes. **These variable results do not establish a no-regression or speedup claim.** Managed allocation, allocated-byte and store counts were identical for every unchanged control in both comparisons.

Selected second-run results, baseline #4517 `bac87e4f` versus final candidate (median / p95 ms):

| Engine / existing workload | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Source Write(string) | 2.5416 / 3.9372 | 2.4624 / 4.2016 |
| Source WriteLine(string) | 3.9317 / 4.9060 | 2.5870 / 3.0343 |
| Source Write(char) | 1.9864 / 2.1752 | 1.6137 / 1.7080 |
| Source whole buffer | 5.2209 / 5.4056 | 4.1360 / 4.3853 |
| CIL Write(string) | 2.4872 / 2.7397 | 1.8091 / 1.8140 |
| CIL WriteLine(string) | 4.3006 / 5.0169 | 3.0772 / 4.0357 |
| CIL whole buffer | 5.5677 / 6.9026 | 4.4464 / 4.9931 |
| CIL buffer slice | 4.4843 / 9.8472 | 4.7671 / 5.0677 |

In that second run, 7/27 source and 11/27 CIL controls exceeded +5% median. New Write(Int64), Write(Double), Write(Decimal) medians were 1.5232 / 1.4507 / 1.4168 ms on source and 1.7864 / 1.6819 / 1.4958 ms on CIL. The runner README gives exact reproduction arguments and interpretation.

The earlier scalar package tarball measured **10,653 bytes**, versus 9,439 bytes for #4517: approximately **12.9% larger**, also exceeding the repository's 10% size budget. Sixteen added overloads and their runtime module explain added scope, but performance/size acceptance still needs explicit review; the inherited 10 KiB target is not claimed.

## Why this remains a draft / concrete remaining steps

1. The original IO package branch needs four workspace/dependency entries in root `package-lock.json`. The live `agent-locks/package-json` lease belongs to `codex-p19-core`, task SF-A25-T01.1 (#2072), generation `8f3f406a-3f3e-4ea7-ac65-258a5b41afe9`, expires 2026-10-04 20:04:09 UTC. The lease is not implicitly taken over; the exact four-entry patch is prepared locally.
2. Once the shared lock is released or explicitly coordinated, apply the minimal lockfile patch on the oldest IO branch and propagate it upward with merges. Run clean installation and each required core check, then merge the stack in order.
3. Resolve the measured performance/size budget review before promoting this batch.

Object and composite-format Write/WriteLine overloads, format-provider callbacks, spans and stream-backed readers/writers remain separate unfinished work. Unsupported members retain diagnostics; no broader BCL or native/Wasm/browser execution parity is claimed.


### Hosted check outcome

[Core run 37202628163](https://github.com/wieslawsoltes/SharpForge/actions/runs/37202628163) failed at `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`, confirming the inherited clean-install blocker above. The preceding contract/seam review passed. The local focused test and build results above are separate from this failed required check.
